#!/usr/bin/env node
import { greeting } from '../src/greet.js';

const name = process.argv.slice(2).find((a) => !a.startsWith('--'));
if (!name) {
  process.stderr.write('usage: greet <name>\n');
  process.exit(2);
}
process.stdout.write(`${greeting(name)}\n`);

result.builder:
Make one pull request for https://github.com/o/greet-cli/issues/12 (--shout flag) that meets these acceptance lines:
1. node bin/greet.js --shout <name> prints the greeting in upper case
2. without --shout the output is unchanged
3. docs/index.md documents --shout
4. after merge, the published docs page at https://o.github.io/greet-cli/ lists --shout

Context: bin/greet.js takes the first argument that does not start with `--` as the name and prints `greeting(name)` from src/greet.js (`Hello, <name>!`). It ignores other `--` arguments right now, so `--shout` currently changes nothing. docs/index.md is the docs page. .github/workflows/pages.yml publishes the docs/ directory to GitHub Pages on every push to main.

Steps:
1. In bin/greet.js, check whether `--shout` is among the arguments (in any position, e.g. `--shout Ada` and `Ada --shout`). If it is, print the whole greeting in upper case (e.g. `HELLO, ADA!`). Keep the name as the first argument that does not start with `--`. Keep the usage error and exit code 2 when no name is given.
2. Do not change the output without --shout: `node bin/greet.js Ada` must still print exactly `Hello, Ada!` plus a newline. Leave the existing tests in test/greet.test.js as they are and make sure they pass.
3. Add tests to test/greet.test.js (node:test, run with `npm test`) for `--shout Ada` -> `HELLO, ADA!\n` and for the plain output staying the same.
4. Update docs/index.md so it documents `--shout`. Show the usage (e.g. `node bin/greet.js --shout <name>`) and say that it prints the greeting in upper case. Spell the flag literally as `--shout` so the published page contains that text.
5. Do not change .github/workflows/pages.yml unless it has to change for docs/ to be published. Line 4 only becomes checkable after merge, once the Pages workflow has run. In the PR description, say that line 4 depends on that workflow publishing docs/index.md after merge.
6. Run `npm test` and the commands above, then open the pull request and link the issue.

text:
I wrote both briefs for issue #12 (`--shout` flag) and the harness accepted them. I changed nothing in the repository.

The fourth acceptance line can't be checked until the pull request is merged. It needs the published page at https://o.github.io/greet-cli/ to list `--shout`, and that page only updates when `.github/workflows/pages.yml` runs on a push to main. Right now it returns HTTP 404. So at the PR head the verifier can only call that line "not yet verifiable", and the brief tells it never to call it PASS. The builder is told to say in the PR description that this line depends on the workflow publishing after merge.

Before the change, I ran every verifier command on the current code:

| Check | Expect line | Command result now |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `--shout <name>` prints upper case | FAILS, as expected: the program ignores `--shout` and still prints `Hello, Ada!` |
| 2 | Output unchanged without `--shout` | PASSES: plain output is `Hello, Ada!` and `npm test` passes |
| 3 | `docs/index.md` documents `--shout` | FAILS, as expected: `docs/index.md` doesn't mention it |
| 4 | Published page lists `--shout` | FAILS, as expected: the page returns HTTP 404 |

None failed because of the command itself.

The builder brief has the builder:
- add `--shout` to `bin/greet.js` so it works before or after the name;
- keep the plain output exactly `Hello, Ada!`;
- add tests;
- document `--shout` in `docs/index.md`.

The verifier brief has one check per expect line, in order. Extra checks are under the Advisory heading: `Ada --shout` as well as `--shout Ada`, the no-name usage error with exit code 2, and new tests.
